title: Tenant credit fractionalization and staggered reset orchestrator
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Reserved customers and high-burst tenants experience sharp throttle events at monthly/day boundaries due to synchronized reset semantics (single-cutover) and coarse-grained quota units. This causes transient customer errors, billing disputes, and inefficient reserved pool utilization.

Proposal: Implement a credit fractionalization layer that slices tenant monthly/daily quotas into micro-credits (fractional tokens) distributed across staggered reset windows (a deterministic, tenant-anchored jitter) plus an orchestrator to coordinate transitions for reserved capacity pools. The orchestrator guarantees: consistent accounting, idempotent resets, predictable allowed burst behavior, and transparent reconciliation for billing.

Key ideas:
- Fractionalization: split a tenant's quota into N micro-credits (configurable; default 144 per day or 720 per month) that replenish incrementally instead of one atomic reset.
- Staggered reset windows: compute per-tenant deterministic offset based on tenant-id and configured anchor (billing zone/timezone preference) to avoid large simultaneous top-ups across tenants and regions.
- Orchestrator responsibilities: maintain micro-credit state, accept consumption events, execute micro-reset ticks, run reconciliation jobs for late/duplicate events, and emit ledger-level delta events used by billing pipeline.
- Reserved pools semantics: when tenants are on Reserved capacity, orchestrator performs a two-phase replenish: micro-credit local top-up + cross-pool lease refresh to avoid overcommitting reserved GPUs.

Goals: reduce midnight spike throttles, avoid mass concurrent top-ups, maintain deterministic ledger events for billing, preserve backward compatibility for existing quota APIs, and allow safe rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: New fractionalized credit model is available behind feature flag 'fractional-quota-v1'
At 100k synthetic tenants, midcut spike rate (errors due to top-up race) decreases by >= 90% during simulated boundary events
Ledger emits identical total-usage per-tenant compared to legacy model within 0.01% over 30-day synthetic replay
Reserved capacity integration prevents transient over-allocations: no reserved pool >100ms over-commit on top-up events during rollout tests
API compatibility: existing quota endpoints return equivalent effective allowance for customers not using the flag
Reconciliation job can correct late events with deterministic rollback messages and produces an audit report consumable by billing jobs
tasks: Design: finalize micro-credit data model and tick frequency (doc: confluence/redwood/quota-fractionalization)
Proto: implement in-memory orchestrator prototype and run local integration with usage-simulator
API: add optional 'fractional' parameter to quota query/consume endpoints; maintain backward-compatible defaults
Runtime: implement micro-reset scheduler with tenant-anchored offset and jitter generator
Reserved path: add two-phase reserve refresh logic for reserved pools and write guard tests
Reconcile: implement reconcile worker that idempotently replays events and emits correction deltas
Telemetry: add metrics, dashboards, and alerts (see telemetry_and_alerting below)
Docs: internal runbook for failure modes and public docs explaining expected behaviour
QA: chaos tests for clock skew, replayed late events, double-consume, and cross-region cutovers
Rollout: staged canary, org opt-in, and global flip after validation
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Lab (2 weeks): prototype and synthetic load testing with usage-simulator (no customer traffic)
Phase 1 - Canary (1 week): enable feature flag for internal / test tenants; monitor top-up behavior and ledger parity
Phase 2 - Opt-in pilot (2 weeks): enable for a small percentage of low-risk customer accounts (5-10%) across regions
Phase 3 - Reserved pilot: enable reserved capacity path for one Dedicated customer and validate no over-commit
Phase 4 - Gradual ramp: increase opt-in percentage while watching error budgets and billing parity metrics
Phase 5 - Global flip: remove flag and default to fractional model after 2-week stable window and billing signoff
telemetry_and_alerting: Metrics to instrument: micro_credit_available, micro_credit_topup_count, micro_reset_latency_ms, micro_reconcile_corrections, reserved_pool_overcommit_ms
Dashboards: per-tenant distribution of top-ups (heatmap), global hourly top-up rate, ledger parity trend vs legacy model
Alerts: >0.1% tenant ledger drift after reconcile run (P0), reserved_pool_overcommit_ms > 200ms sustained for 1m (P1), spike in micro_reset_latency_ms (P1)
Tracing: add trace spans for orchestrator tick -> ledger write -> billing emission to correlate latency spikes
notes: Trade-offs: fractionalization increases event volume to billing (N micro-events vs 1 macro-event). Mitigation: compress micro-deltas in the billing pipeline into batched deltas before invoicing.

Edge cases: handling tenants that change quotas mid-cycle (plan upgrades) requires pro-rated redistribution of remaining micro-credits; design includes a conversion routine executed at plan change time.
Clock skew & replay: reconciler must treat late client events as consumptions against the next available micro-credit and emit correction deltas when necessary.
Backwards compatibility: default behaviour remains unchanged unless flag enabled; SDKs should not be forced to change but can opt-in for lower burst errors.
Performance: in-memory caches keyed by tenant will hold micro-credit counters; we limit hot-tenant memory by using LRU eviction and persistent checkpointing of hot shards.
